name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
principle: Attacker-controlled data is inserted into a structured output message without correct encoding for that output context. Special characters then become control data or metadata, so the receiver interprets the message with altered structure or commands.
detection_signals: Untrusted input is concatenated into HTML, XML, HTTP headers, SQL, shell commands, or protocol strings before the sink call.
Manual escaping uses chained `replace()` calls or a blacklist of special characters instead of a vetted encoder.
The same tainted value is reused in multiple output contexts but encoded only once with one generic routine.
A context-mismatched encoder is used, such as `URLEncoder.encode()` for HTML output or HTML escaping before `exec()`/`system()`.
Custom sanitizer omits known metacharacters like `;`, `|`, `&`, `\r`, `\n`, `'`, `"`, `<`, `>`.
Header/log/message construction uses raw concatenation into `setHeader()`, `println()`, `write()`, `append()`, or template output without a final encode step.
negative_signals: A vetted, context-specific encoder is applied immediately before the sink, such as `StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4()` or `OWASP Encoder.encodeForHTML()` for HTML output.
Structured APIs are used instead of string building, such as `PreparedStatement` with `?` parameters or other parameterized interfaces.
The sink only receives hard-coded constants or values proven not to be attacker-controlled.
Limited markup is allowed only through an explicit allowlist sanitizer, followed by syntax validation of the resulting output.
The component explicitly sets and matches character encoding at the interface, such as `setCharacterEncoding("UTF-8")`, and uses the same encoding end-to-end.
false_defense_traps: Blacklisting only a few characters and assuming all dangerous metacharacters are covered.
Using URL encoding, HTML encoding, or shell escaping in the wrong output context.
Encoding first and then later decoding, normalizing, or re-concatenating the value before the final sink.
Relying on input validation alone when the same data is emitted to multiple downstream parsers.
Stripping tags or punctuation but leaving delimiter characters that the target parser still treats as control input.
verification_focus: Is every attacker-controlled field encoded exactly for the final output context at the last sink, with no later decode or unsafe concatenation?

consequence_chains.trigger: Untrusted data is written into HTML/JavaScript without context-correct escaping
consequence_chains.consequence: Cross-site scripting and client-side script execution

consequence_chains.trigger: Untrusted data is written into a log line without CR/LF escaping
Untrusted data is inserted into a shell command without shell escaping

patch_principle: Use a vetted output-encoding library for the exact sink context.
Prefer parameterized or structured APIs that separate data from control syntax.
Apply encoding at the final output boundary, not earlier in the data flow.
Use strict allowlists only when control syntax must be partially permitted, then verify the final syntax.
Keep character encodings explicit and consistent across component interfaces.
